title: STORY-1656 Tenant IT Admin ownership transfer and lifecycle (BUG-1469, TASK-1657, TASK-1658)
answer_key: 17 concerns reconstructed from the work records (decisions.json, requirements, investigation.md), plus the 3 comments the user named as the client reviewer's. It is NOT the client's review thread.
limitation: The reviewer had already seen the recorded findings and had reviewed this story before sealing, so no run on this story can be blind. The branches hold one squashed commit that already contains the fixes for review findings 1, 2, 6, 7, 10 and the delete/transfer race: those concerns can only be derived as a risk class from this code. Severity is recorded only where the record or the user states it.

concerns.text: The IT Admin email guard turns a null or blank email into a misleading 'email cannot be changed' error instead of leaving it to the normal 'Email is required' validation.
concerns.consequence: A user sees a wrong reason for a rejected edit; validation behavior of existing endpoints changes.
concerns.unsupported_state: none (wrong error)

concerns.text: The transfer looked the caller up by email, which can throw on case-variant duplicate rows or match another tenant; caller authorization must be by id, and the caller's tenant must be the acting tenant or an ancestor.
concerns.consequence: A legitimate parent administrator fails, or the wrong user is authorized.
concerns.unsupported_state: caller resolved to the wrong or no user

concerns.text: Concurrent transfers from the same IT Admin could both succeed and leave two IT Admins.
concerns.consequence: A tenant with two IT Admins; every rule that assumes exactly one is wrong.
concerns.unsupported_state: two IT Admins

concerns.text: The transfer action was hidden from parent (MSSP) administrators because the UI looked the caller up in the tenant's own user list.
concerns.consequence: A parent administrator the server allows never sees the action.
concerns.unsupported_state: an allowed actor cannot act

must_match: fallback when nothing is found: return self \? isPortalAdminUser\(self\) : true

concerns.text: Stale grid after a failed transfer.
concerns.entity: Portal Access UI / grid and dialog
concerns.consequence: The user acts on data the server has already changed.
concerns.unsupported_state: stale state offered for action

concerns.text: deleteUser read the default-user flag without a lock: a delete racing a transfer could remove the user who had just become IT Admin, including their Keycloak account, leaving the tenant with no IT Admin.
concerns.consequence: A tenant with no IT Admin and a deleted identity.
concerns.unsupported_state: tenant with no IT Admin

concerns.text: The IT Admin row shows '-' for Created: tenants-api builds the admin without createdAt, updatedAt or createdBy.
concerns.consequence: The audit metadata of the provisioned IT Admin is missing now that the row is visible.
concerns.unsupported_state: an owner row without audit history

concerns.text: Single source of truth: the tenant IT Admin must be resolved everywhere from the transferred ownership state (users.default_user); the new owner must be reflected consistently across the platform.
concerns.consequence: Different services show or authorize different owners.
concerns.unsupported_state: services disagree about who the owner is

concerns.text: The Tenant Details Admin Email must always represent the current Tenant IT Admin; the Portal Access IT Admin and the Tenant Details Admin Email must never point to different people.
concerns.consequence: The portal shows different owners in different places.
concerns.unsupported_state: tenant email and owner disagree

concerns.text: Exactly one defaultUser per tenant is enforced in code, not by a database constraint.
concerns.consequence: Any writer that bypasses the code path can create two or zero IT Admins.
concerns.unsupported_state: two or zero IT Admins

concerns.text: Tenants whose tenant.email already differs from their IT Admin's email stay misaligned until their first transfer (no backfill).
concerns.consequence: Existing production tenants behave differently from new ones.
concerns.unsupported_state: legacy tenants violate the new rule

concerns.text: Tenant.email is written from sfn-iam-api and this assumes a shared database with sfn-tenants-api; not verified that every environment uses the same database.
concerns.consequence: A transfer silently depends on the deployment topology and the owner's schema.
concerns.unsupported_state: transfer fails or diverges where databases differ

concerns.text: Ownership transfer moves only the IT Admin identity (defaultUser) while Portal Administration capabilities come from group membership: a transfer to any ACTIVE user can leave the new IT Admin without Portal Administration permissions while the previous owner stays an administrator.
concerns.consequence: Identity and capability drift apart.
concerns.unsupported_state: owner without admin capability

concerns.text: Updating tenant.email to the new owner's email changes the tenant's email domain, which three services treat as always-allowed for extension enrollment and which the portal uses to block cross-domain user creation.
concerns.consequence: Who may enroll extensions and create users changes silently when the owner changes.
concerns.unsupported_state: enrollment allow-list changes with the owner

concerns.text: Editing the IT Admin's email in Portal Access changes users.email and Keycloak but not tenant.email, so the tenant email and the IT Admin can drift apart.
concerns.consequence: The mirrored email diverges through the second writer.
concerns.unsupported_state: tenant email and owner disagree

concerns.text: Not verified: whether other screens that list users call GET /users and now show the IT Admin.
concerns.consequence: Counts, dropdowns and selection lists elsewhere change.
concerns.unsupported_state: other screens show an extra record

concerns.text: Not verified: whether tenants-api tenant deprovisioning removes users in a way that bypasses the new delete guard.
concerns.consequence: Deleting a tenant removes its IT Admin with no guard, ownership or audit step.
concerns.unsupported_state: IT Admin removed outside the guarded path

concerns.text: The IT Admin can be deactivated.
concerns.consequence: The owner becomes inactive; platform-admin recognition (which needs an ACTIVE default user) disappears, so operators lose platform access.
concerns.unsupported_state: inactive owner / platform without an active default user

must_match: UserService\.java:\d+\s+updateUser\s+<- does not mention the flag

concerns.source: named by the user as comments of the client reviewer (Raghu); the wording is a headline, not the original text

concerns.text: The IT Admin can be removed from the admin group.
concerns.consequence: The owner loses administration capability, and with no other Portal Administrator nobody can transfer ownership.
concerns.unsupported_state: owner without permissions; tenant with no Portal Administrator
concerns.source: named by the user as comments of the client reviewer (Raghu); the wording is a headline, not the original text

concerns.text: The new IT Admin is not promoted into the admin group during ownership transfer.
concerns.consequence: Ownership and authority drift: the new owner cannot administer while the former owner keeps the capability.
concerns.unsupported_state: owner without permissions; capability held by a non-owner
concerns.source: named by the user as comments of the client reviewer (Raghu); the wording is a headline, not the original text
